My strategic approach considers multiple factors:
1. My true preference order is y > z > w > x
2. I have high priority (rank 1) at both y and w
3. Most applicants favor y > x > w > z, which might increase competition at y

Key strategic considerations:
- If y is very competitive due to high applicant preference, I might get rejected
- In that case, z is my next most preferred school
- z has a priority rank of 2, which means I have a backup option
- If I'm rejected from y and z, I'll then propose to w (where I also have high priority)
- x is my least preferred option, so I'll only go there if all other options fail

This means my optimal strategy is to rank schools: y > z > w > x
This preserves my true preference order while providing strategic fallback options
